Pub food at it's finest

 

Perfectly positioned by the river in the heart of Cambridge, The Mill is the ideal spot for traditional British pub food. Whether you’re refuelling after a walk along the Cam, meeting friends for a relaxed meal, or searching for a standout Sunday roast, there’s something for everyone to enjoy in a warm and welcoming setting.

Sip Into Winter

Make the most of the colder months with a cocktail made for the season. Our winter cocktail menu brings together warming flavours, seasonal ingredients and plenty of character, with serves designed for everything from a catch-up with friends to a cosy evening by the river. So settle in, pick your favourite and let us take care of the rest.

Gather round for Sunday lunch

Sundays are made for taking your time over a proper roast. Tuck into tender meats, crispy roasties, seasonal vegetables, plenty of gravy and all the trimmings.

Settle in with your favourite people and meet your Sunday sidekick: a Bloody Mary made in partnership with The Pickle House. Their signature mix, complete with Absolut Tabasco, brings a bold, spicy kick that’s just the thing alongside your roast. Good food, good drinks and plenty of time to relax.

Christmas Feasting

Celebrate the flavours of the season at The Mill with festive menus created by our talented chefs using the very best seasonal produce.

From relaxed Christmas lunches to indulgent festive feasts, every dish is crafted to bring people together. Pair your meal with carefully selected wines, local beers or handcrafted cocktails and make every Christmas gathering one to remember.

Seasonal Flavours

At The Mill, we believe great food starts with fresh, seasonal ingredients. Our menus celebrate the best of British produce, brought to life by our talented kitchen team. With a focus on quality and flavour, we offer a welcoming riverside spot for simple, well-crafted dishes.

Host Something Special

From casual get-togethers to private drinks or meetings in the Snug, we’ve got the perfect space to host your occasion.
